preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 500,000) representing the number of acorns in the tree.
The second line contains exactly 2n - 1 integers (or 0s) representing the Euler tour sequence.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(x) <= int(stdin.split()[0]) for x in stdin.split()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each element in the sequence is either 0 (illegible) or an integer between 1 and n (inclusive).

postconditions.description: If no valid Euler tour exists, output 'no'. Otherwise, output 'yes' followed by a valid Euler tour sequence of length 2n - 1.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'yes' and all(1 <= int(x) <= int(stdin.split()[0]) for x in stdout.split()[1:])
postconditions.description: If 'yes' is output, the Euler tour sequence must consist of integers between 1 and n (inclusive).
If 'yes' is output, the first and last elements of the Euler tour must be the same.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'yes' and all(1 <= int(x) <= int(stdin.split()[0]) for x in stdout.split()[1:]) and all(int(x) in {1, 2, ..., int(stdin.split()[0])} for x in stdout.split()[1:])
postconditions.description: If 'yes' is output, every acorn number from 1 to n must appear at least once in the Euler tour.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'yes' and all(1 <= int(x) <= int(stdin.split()[0]) for x in stdout.split()[1:]) and all(1 <= int(y) <= int(stdin.split()[0]) for y in stdout.split()[1:]) and all(abs(int(x) - int(y)) == 1 or (int(x) != 0 and int(y) != 0 and int(x) != int(y)) for x, y in zip(stdout.split()[1:], stdout.split()[2:]))
postconditions.description: If 'yes' is output, the Euler tour must be a valid sequence where consecutive acorns are directly connected by a branch (i.e., the sequence must correspond to a valid traversal of a tree).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'yes' and all(int(x) == int(y) or int(x) != 0 or int(y) != 0 for x, y in zip(stdin.split()[1:], stdout.split()[1:]))
postconditions.description: If 'yes' is output, the output Euler tour must match the input sequence where the input is not 0 (i.e., non-illegible entries must remain unchanged).
